::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
The emblematic China fab-boom failure and this tracker's first explicit Cancelled entry (the schema always had the status): a 90%-shell-owned '128-billion-yuan 14nm' project that spent ~¥15.3 billion by end-2019, staged a fake production line for investors, took delivery of an ASML NXT:1980Di DUV scanner (repeatedly misreported in Chinese media as 'EUV') in Dec 2019, and mortgaged it for ¥580 million in Jan 2020.
:::

**Chinese name:** 武汉弘芯半导体制造有限公司 (Wǔhàn Hóngxīn Bàndǎotǐ)

## What does this facility make?

Nothing — unfinished shells and two vacant dormitory towers; state takeover Nov 2020, staff cut Feb 2021, renamed 武汉新工现代制造 and deregistered 29 June 2021.

## Why does it matter?

HSMC triggered the 2020-21 central-level cleanup of rogue semiconductor pledges and the 'new-type举国体制' debate over local-government fab financing; site reuse as of 2025-26 is not verified. Keeping cancelled projects in the tracker matters: the denominator of announced Chinese fabs is as analytically important as the operational numerator.

## Project Timeline

- **Nov 2017** — Registered in Wuhan Linkonggang (Dongxihu) with claimed ¥128B plan
- **Dec 2019** — ASML NXT:1980Di DUV tool arrives — the only major tool ever delivered
- **Nov 2020** — State takes over; company deregistered 29 June 2021
